Real past bmo reactions computed from Yahoo daily closes: Nov-24 -5.1, Mar-25 -9.2, May-25 +14.7, Aug-25 -1.4, Nov-25 +37.5, Mar-26 -3.6, May-26 +8.9, Aug-26 +35.7 (median abs 9.1%). The baseline's 2025 rows are tagged amc and record the day after, so they understate the moves. Run-up: the stock went from 108.90 before the Q2 print to a 171.09 high on 2026-11-04, then fell to 137.64 (2026-11-19, the day Gap cut its Q4 outlook on warm weather), and was 144.32 intraday today; -13.9% over 20 days. Consensus (Yahoo, read 2026-11-23): Q3 EPS 3.15 (3.21 a week ago) against a guide of 2.90-3.20 (whisper 3.22); Q3 revenue 1.37B at the top of the 1.355-1.368B guide; Q4 EPS 4.87 against about 4.71 implied by the guide midpoint (range 4.31-5.11, own arithmetic: FY 13.10-13.60 minus YTD 5.59 minus Q3 guide); Q4 revenue 1.78B (+6.8%), which matches the roughly +7% Q4 implied by the 'around 5%' FY guide on H1 actuals of 1.11B and 1.27B. FY consensus 13.56 sits in the top half of the guide. FY28 estimate cut 13.39 to 13.15 in the last week. Short interest 12.1% of float, 4.3 days to cover (2026-10-30 settlement, rising from 9.0% on 07-31). Sell side leans bullish: UBS target $200 (11-11), Goldman buy at $180 and has raised its Hollister comp to flat on better intraquarter sales and EU traffic; mean target about $171.
view: ANF will very likely beat its Q3 EPS guide again. It beat the top of guide in Q4-25, Q1-26 ($1.47 against 1.20-1.30) and Q2-26 ($2.42 excluding the refund against 1.80-2.00). August foot traffic (Advan, FQ3 quarter-to-date +7% for Abercrombie, +3% for Hollister on the observable US footprint), October indoor-mall traffic (+4.1%, Placer) and Goldman's intraquarter read all support a solid quarter. All of that is the expected path, though: consensus and the whisper already sit above the guide midpoint, and the stock has made 35-38% upside moves on its last two Q3/Q2-type beats, which everyone remembers. The reaction will turn on the Q4/holiday guide and comps. The Street's Q4 (EPS 4.87, sales +6.8%) already asks for a sales acceleration from flat comps. The freshest datapoint, Gap's 2026-11-19 release ('demand softened in October and early November amidst warmer weather', Q4 guided flat to -1%), echoed by TJX on cold-weather categories, argues for a cautious ANF Q4 framing. Freight and ERP costs were flagged as back-half drags. A 'beat Q3 and pass through only the beat' guide would leave Q4 implied below 4.87: the Nov-2024 pattern (opened +3%, closed -5%). Against that, the stock already fell 6.4% on Gap's day and 20% from its high, the put skew already pays for this fear, 12% of float is short and rising, and ANF has a $500M buyback. A clean beat with the FY guide raised to about 13.6-13.8 could still squeeze it, as in Nov-2025 when it was depressed. The evidence on both sides is public and visibly in the price (the Gap-day drop, the skew, estimates that already sit above guide), so I cannot show an unpriced direction. I am close to a coin flip with a slight upward tilt from the beat pattern plus short positioning, and expect a large move either way.

recommendation.reason: A Q3 beat is likely but is the consensus path (estimates and whisper above the guide midpoint, and the history of beats is well known). The deciding line is the Q4 guide. The one fresh negative datapoint, Gap's warm-weather softness through early November, already cost ANF 6.4% on 2026-11-19 and sits in a 17-point put skew, so I cannot show either side is unpriced. No mechanism clears the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 guide implying EPS at or above about 4.9 with commentary that November trends are on plan (or Hollister comps clearly positive) would make me lean long, given 12% short interest. A Q4 implied below about 4.6, or an FY sales growth cut below 5% citing weather, would make me lean short.

self_critique: The case for a lean: ANF has beaten its own guide by wide margins three quarters running, the Street's Q3 number embeds almost none of that, 12% of float is short, and the stock is 20% off its high. Its last two comparable setups produced +37% and +36% days, so a no-call may be leaving the most predictable feature of this name on the table. On the other side, the stock is not depressed as it was at $65 in Nov-2025, sentiment and targets are bullish, and the Gap/TJX weather read plus freight point to a cautious holiday guide, which killed the Nov-2024 rally by midday. Both cases are public and I cannot show which one the price underweights.
approach_notes: P4 (prove priced-in) helped: the Gap read-through looked like an edge until the 11-19 price drop and the skew showed it was already taken. P6's 'find the line' pointed to the Q4 guide, and the own-arithmetic check of guide-implied Q4 against consensus was the most useful step. The baseline's history rows are mis-tagged amc for 2025 and understate past moves; recomputing them from bars mattered.
